disclaimer: Reminder reference only - NOT legal authority. Season dates, zones, and limits are set annually and can change. Always verify current regulations with the Ontario Ministry of Natural Resources before hunting or trapping. Trapping in Ontario is governed by the Fish and Wildlife Conservation Act, 1997 and O. Reg. 667/98 (Trapping) and O. Reg. 670/98 (Open Seasons - Wildlife). This dataset is for the separate Canada clone of Opossum Foot; it is NOT part of the US app, which stays US-only and untouched.

license_summary.certified_traps: Only AIHTS-certified traps may be used for species listed in Schedule 1 (killing traps) and Schedule 2 (restraining traps) of O. Reg. 667/98 (s. 18). See the 'aihts' section of this dataset.
license_summary.course: Fur Harvest, Fur Management and Conservation Course (40 hours: 32 classroom + 8 hands-on) completed within the last 5 years; required for a first trapping licence (O. Reg. 667/98 s. 11).
license_summary.fees: Trapping licence $39.55; secondary (helper/youth) $16.95 (HST included). Outdoors Card $8.57 + HST.
license_summary.harvest_report: Mandatory Season-End Harvest Report: record the quantity of each species harvested within 24 hours of the close of the season for that species; submit by June 10 to the Ontario Fur Managers Federation or the applicable Provincial Treaty Organization (s. 13).
license_summary.hunting_furbearers: Arctic fox, raccoon, opossum, red fox, skunk and weasel may also be hunted under a Small Game Licence (Hunting Summary pp. 88-89). Wolf and coyote may be hunted under a Small Game Licence plus a Wolf/Coyote Tag in WMUs where a tag is required (max 2 tags per calendar year). A CITES export permit is required to export wolves from Canada. Furbearing mammals generally may not be hunted in provincial parks or Crown Game Preserves.
license_summary.licence_types: Landowner, resident, head trapper (Registered Trapline Area), helper trapper, youth. Only one registered trapline area per licence (s. 9).
license_summary.licensing_transition: The Fish and Wildlife Licensing Service (huntandfishontario.com) is being replaced by FishHuntON, launching December 10, 2026; the current system is unavailable December 7-9, 2026 (ontario.ca, October 30, 2026). Licence URLs in this dataset may go stale within a month of the retrieval date.
license_summary.otter_incidental: An otter taken out of season may only be possessed if it was incidentally killed while lawfully trapping beaver despite all due diligence, and the incident is recorded on the season-end harvest report (Trapping Regulations Summary, Pelt possession).
license_summary.permission: Trap only on land designated on the licence; written landowner permission required on private land (s. 8).
license_summary.quotas: Harvest quotas are fixed on the licence and are licence-specific (s. 6). Trapping less than 75% of the beaver quota fixed by the licence is an offence and can mean the licence is not renewed (s. 7). There are no bag limits in Table 6; harvest is governed by licence quotas.
license_summary.report_violation: MNR TIPS line 1-877-847-7667 (1-877-TIPS-MNR); anonymous via Crime Stoppers 1-800-222-TIPS (8477). Natural Resources Information and Support Centre: 1-800-387-7011.
license_summary.trap_check: Every live-holding trap must be inspected at least once a day (s. 25(3)), except in the parts of Ontario north of the most northerly east-west CNR line / Calstock-Nakina forest access road (s. 25(4)).
license_summary.trapping_licence: A trapping licence is required (O. Reg. 667/98). Adult: 16+, Ontario resident or Canadian citizen, valid Outdoors Card, hunter accreditation on file, and the Fur Harvest, Fur Management and Conservation Course completed within the last 5 years (40 hours: 32 classroom + 8 hands-on). Youth 12-15: course + parental consent, under direct supervision of a licensed trapper 18+. Trapping licences are paper applications to the MNR work centre; payment to the Ontario Fur Managers Federation or the applicable Provincial Treaty Organization.
license_summary.wolf_coyote_reporting: A wolf or coyote killed in WMUs 1-10, 11A, 11B, 12-42, 46-50 or 53-58 in protection of property must be reported immediately to a ministry office unless a Notice of Possession is submitted. Wolf/coyote tag holders must submit a mandatory hunter report (deadline January 14, 2027 for the 2026 season).

aihts.models_note: This pass captured schedule structure and approximate model counts per species, not the full model-by-model list. Full transcription of Schedules 1 and 2 is a defined follow-on task (see the scoping report). Certification is not the same as current manufacturing: several certified models are legacy/discontinued. Do not present the certified list as a shopping list without a retailer-availability check.
aihts.note: Ontario implements AIHTS through O. Reg. 667/98 ss. 18-18.1 and Schedules 1 (certified killing traps) and 2 (certified restraining traps). A 'certified trap' is a killing trap listed in Schedule 1 column 3 or a restraining trap listed in Schedule 2 column 3 for that species (s. 1(1)). The Fur Institute of Canada maintains the national certified-trap list (updated July 22, 2026); Ontario's schedules are drawn from it. AIHTS was agreed in 1997 and ratified by Canada in June 1999; it covers 12 North American species. Phase 1 regulated species match Ontario's schedules; Phase 2 species are not yet regulated.
trap_rules: Only certified traps may be used for species listed in Schedules 1 and 2 (O. Reg. 667/98 s. 18).
Body-gripping traps with jaw spread over 22 cm are banned in WMUs 60-95 except in-water beaver/otter sets (s. 18.1(2)).

Leg-hold traps may only be used as permitted by s. 19: coyote and fox within size limits; beaver, muskrat, otter and mink in submersion sets; red squirrel in enclosed killing sets; certified leg-holds for raccoon, lynx and bobcat.
No leg-hold traps for fisher, marten, opossum, skunk or weasel.
Leg-hold jaw spread: max 18 cm on land, 21 cm in water; 23 cm for wolf with a certified trap (s. 24).
Trap chain max 31 cm (s. 25(1)); live-holding traps inspected at least once daily (s. 25(3)), except north of the CNR line (s. 25(4)).
Black bear: foot snares, box or culvert traps only (s. 20); no trapping within 400 m of a waste disposal site (s. 22).
Night dispatch of trapped animals: rim-fire firearm only (s. 27.1).

aihts.canada_wide: AIHTS in force in Canada since 1 June 1999 (Canada, the EU and Russia are parties; the US is not a party). FIC-certified traps mandatory per Phase 1 lists - killing traps: beaver, Canada lynx & bobcat, fisher, marten, muskrat (on land and underwater), otter, raccoon, weasels/ermine; restraining traps: beaver (cage), bobcat, Canada lynx, raccoon, wolf. Conventional steel-jawed leghold restraining traps on land are effectively banned for AIHTS species. Killing neck snares are NOT AIHTS traps and are not FIC-certified; provinces regulate snares separately. [R1 s.2a]
aihts.jurisdiction_specific: Exclusive use of certified restraining traps for raccoon is mandatory in Ontario (FIC list Note 1 provinces: ON, QC, PEI, NB, NS). Ontario implements AIHTS through O. Reg. 667/98 ss. 18-18.1 and Schedules 1 (certified killing) and 2 (certified restraining). [R1 s.2a]

check_interval.live_holding: Daily - every live-holding trap south of the most northerly east-west CN Rail line (O. Reg. 667/98 s. 25(3)); relaxing cable restraints daily everywhere.
check_interval.killing: No general check interval stated in the sources.

canada_only.tenure: Registered trapline areas on Crown land (allocated by the Ministry as vacancies occur) plus private-land (landowner) licences; licence is area-specific and carries licence-specific quotas.
canada_only.trap_id_requirement: None found - no trap owner-ID marking requirement in the sources searched (follow-up pass, Nov 17); identification runs through licence/tenure and pelt seals instead. Near-miss: containers used to transport pelts must be marked with contents and consignor/consignee name and address - shipment marking, not trap marking.
canada_only.royalty: Royalty on pelts transported out of Ontario: 5.5% of the average Ontario auction price, payable before transport (O. Reg. 666/98 s. 32); an export licence is also required. [R2 Item 5; R1 s.5]
canada_only.nuisance_route: Paid route exists - FWCA s. 31 protection of property: an owner may harass, capture or kill damaging wildlife on their own land and may use an agent. Prescribed agent classes (O. Reg. 665/98 s. 132) include licensed trappers and persons whose business is primarily removing nuisance wildlife - but business-class agents may only harass or capture-and-release, NOT kill. Live-captured animals not killed must be released within 24 hours, within ~1 km of capture. Others act under a Minister's Term Agent Authorization (ongoing) or Individual Agent Authorization (one-off). [R1 s.4]
canada_only.harvest_reporting_and_sealing: Mandatory Season-End Harvest Report: record harvest within 24 hours of season close; submit by June 10 with numbers harvested, sold/shipped and remaining in possession, to OFMF or the applicable Provincial Treaty Organization. Failure is an offence. [R1 s.5]
